Design document: LLM-Based User Profile System from Browser Behavioral Signals
Purpose: infer interests, preferences, identity and short-term context from Edge browser signals, summarize into a 5-layer structured profile with LLMs, and serve that profile in real time to personalize assistant responses. The system stores ONLY derived profile layers (no raw behavioral data persisted).

TABLE OF CONTENTS
1) Full Profile Schema (JSON schemas + examples + layer relationships)
2) Generation Pipeline (per-layer inputs, LLM prompt templates, triggers, and merge strategies)
3) Storage & Serving Architecture (tech, data model, caching, sync/async flows)
4) LLM Summarization Pipeline (batching, model choices, example L3 prompt, parsing, failures)
5) Evaluation Framework (offline/online metrics, A/B test design, privacy checks)
6) Open questions and tradeoffs

---------------------------------------------------------------------
1) FULL PROFILE SCHEMA (JSON / pseudo-JSON)
All timestamps are ISO8601. Each profile is a single JSON blob per user; layers are nested objects. Top-level minimal shape:

{
  "user_id": "UUID",
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "last_updated": "2026-04-18T12:00:00Z",
  "layers": {
    "L1_identity": { ... },
    "L2_preferences": { ... },
    "L3_interests": { ... },
    "L4_world_context": { ... },
    "L5_interest_cards": [ ... ]
  },
  "meta": {
    "version": 42,
    "consent_flags": { "profile_enabled": true, "explicit_prefs_saved": true },
    "staleness": { "L1":"30d", "L2":"7d", "L3":"1d", "L4":"1d", "L5":"48h" }
  }
}

Notes:
- Profile size target ≈ 2 KB average per user (compact strings, tag-style topics, truncated evidence summaries).
- Only derived values stored. No raw URLs, no raw text excerpts. Store domain-level or topic-level signals, small evidence summaries generated by LLMs.
- All fields must include a confidence [0.0-1.0].

L1 — Identity (monthly, stable)
Schema:
{
  "last_updated": "timestamp",
  "confidence": float,
  "occupation": {
    "title": string,                // e.g. "Software Engineer"
    "seniority": string|null,       // e.g. "Senior"
    "confidence": float
  },
  "primary_expertise": [           // ranked
    {
      "tag": string,               // canonical tag: "Machine Learning"
      "confidence": float,
      "last_evidence": "timestamp",
      "evidence_summary": string   // short: "Repeated visits to ML repos/articles"
    }
  ],
  "communication_style": {
    "preferred_tone": "formal|neutral|informal",
    "preferred_length": "short|medium|long",
    "use_bullets": boolean,
    "emoji_tolerance": "low|medium|high",
    "confidence": float
  },
  "explicit_overrides": { /* fields set by user and must not be auto-overwritten */ }
}

Example:
"L1_identity": {
  "last_updated": "2026-04-01T08:00:00Z",
  "confidence": 0.92,
  "occupation": { "title": "Software Engineer", "seniority": "Senior", "confidence": 0.94 },
  "primary_expertise":[
    {"tag":"Machine Learning","confidence":0.96,"last_evidence":"2026-03-30T09:15:00Z",
     "evidence_summary":"Frequent visits to ML blogs, saved tutorial on transfer learning"}
  ],
  "communication_style":{"preferred_tone":"neutral","preferred_length":"short","use_bullets":true,"emoji_tolerance":"low","confidence":0.87},
  "explicit_overrides": {}
}

Relation to other layers:
- L1 is stable: informs personalization defaults (tone, suggested depth). L2/L3 can temporarily override in-session.

L2 — Preferences (weekly)
Schema:
{
  "last_updated":"timestamp",
  "confidence":float,
  "preferred_content_length": "short|medium|long" OR { "min_words": int, "max_words": int },
  "preferred_formality": "formal|neutral|informal",
  "format_preferences": [ "article","video","podcast","code_snippet" ],
  "topics_to_avoid": [ { "tag":string, "confidence":float } ],
  "notification_window": { "quiet_hours": "22:00-07:00", "timezone": string },
  "accessibility_needs": { "large_text": boolean, "screen_reader": boolean },
  "explicit_overrides": { ... }
}

Example:
"L2_preferences": {
  "last_updated":"2026-04-18T06:00:00Z",
  "confidence":0.88,
  "preferred_content_length":"short",
  "preferred_formality":"informal",
  "format_preferences":["article","video"],
  "topics_to_avoid":[ {"tag":"celebrity_gossip","confidence":0.95} ],
  "notification_window":{"quiet_hours":"23:00-06:30","timezone":"America/Los_Angeles"},
  "accessibility_needs":{"large_text":false,"screen_reader":false},
  "explicit_overrides":{ "preferred_formality":"formal" }
}

Relation to others:
- L2 narrows how assistant formats replies. User explicit overrides in L2 supersede auto-generated L1 behavior for the same fields.

L3 — Interests (daily)
Schema:
{
  "last_updated":"timestamp",
  "clusters": [
    {
      "cluster_id": "UUID",
      "label": string,                 // canonical short label, e.g. "LoRA Fine-Tuning"
      "topics": [ string ],            // tags/keywords
      "confidence": float,             // overall cluster confidence
      "intensity": float,              // 0..1 measure of current activity
      "last_activity":"timestamp",
      "decay_half_life_days": int,     // used for temporal decay
      "sample_evidence_summary": string,
      "usage_hints": [ string ]        // 1-3 short hints for personalization
    }
  ],
  "total_active": int
}

Example:
"L3_interests": {
  "last_updated":"2026-04-18T11:30:00Z",
  "clusters":[
    {
      "cluster_id":"c-1029",
      "label":"Transformer Fine-Tuning",
      "topics":["fine-tuning","LoRA","transfer learning","Hugging Face"],
      "confidence":0.95,
      "intensity":0.88,
      "last_activity":"2026-04-18T11:15:00Z",
      "decay_half_life_days":7,
      "sample_evidence_summary":"Searched 'fine-tune llama', visited huggingface.co and highlighted LoRA article",
      "usage_hints":["Show short code snippets","Offer quick examples and links to repos"]
    },
    { ... }
  ],
  "total_active": 4
}

Relation:
- L3 is the main personalization signal (topics to inject into assistant prompts). L4 may temporarily bump or deprioritize clusters for the session.

L4 — World Context (daily)
Schema:
{
  "last_updated":"timestamp",
  "active_projects":[
    {
      "project_id":"UUID",
      "title":string,
      "description":string,
      "status":"planning|in_progress|stalled|complete",
      "relevance_score":float,
      "related_topics":[string],
      "last_activity":"timestamp"
    }
  ],
  "recent_searches_summary":[ string ],
  "open_tabs_summary":[ string (domain or topic) ],
  "top_news_topics":[ { "topic":string, "relevance":float } ],
  "locale": string,
  "timezone": string
}

Example:
"L4_world_context": {
  "last_updated":"2026-04-18T11:45:00Z",
  "active_projects":[
    {"project_id":"p-77","title":"Q2 ML talk","description":"Slide deck on model compression","status":"in_progress","relevance_score":0.90,"related_topics":["Model Compression"],"last_activity":"2026-04-17T21:00:00Z"}
  ],
  "recent_searches_summary":["model compression examples","LoRA tuning best practices"],
  "open_tabs_summary":["github repo (ml)","arXiv paper (model compression)"],
  "top_news_topics":[ {"topic":"Model compression techniques","relevance":0.68} ],
  "locale":"en-US",
  "timezone":"America/Los_Angeles"
}

Relation:
- L4 is ephemeral context used to bias assistant replies during a session. It is overwritten frequently.

L5 — Interest Cards (event-triggered, transient, expire after 48h)
Card schema:
{
  "card_id":"UUID",
  "created_at":"timestamp",
  "expires_at":"timestamp",            // <= created_at + 48h
  "trigger_type": "search_burst|highlight_followup|bookmark_annotation|custom",
  "title": string,
  "summary": string,                   // single-sentence action-oriented summary
  "topics":[ string ],
  "confidence": float,
  "recommended_actions":[              // small actionable suggestions
     { "label": string, "action_type": "open|search|compose|snippet|save", "payload": { ... } }
  ],
  "evidence_count": int,
  "evidence_summary": string
}

Example card:
{
  "card_id":"card-33",
  "created_at":"2026-04-18T10:12:00Z",
  "expires_at":"2026-04-20T10:12:00Z",
  "trigger_type":"highlight_followup",
  "title":"Quick LoRA guide & snippets",
  "summary":"You highlighted LoRA content and did searches on fine-tuning — short how-to and code snippets ready.",
  "topics":["LoRA","fine-tuning"],
  "confidence":0.93,
  "recommended_actions":[ {"label":"Insert snippet","action_type":"snippet","payload":{"lang":"python","code_id":"s-12"}} ],
  "evidence_count":3,
  "evidence_summary":"highlight + 2 searches within 2 hours"
}

Relation:
- L5 drives immediate assistant micro-actions (suggest snippets, follow-ups). Cards are ephemeral and not folded into L1-L3 unless the summarizer finds sustained activity.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
2) GENERATION PIPELINE (how each layer is generated)
Principles:
- Minimize server-side receipt of raw behavioral data: where possible, client (Edge) aggregates/sanitizes events and sends only derived features (top N domains, hashed/cleaned query keywords, counts, semantic n-grams).
- Use hybrid pipeline: inexpensive deterministic feature extraction + embeddings/clustering => LLM labeling/summarization (reduces LLM calls & tokens).
- Each layer has its own cadence and merge rule.

L1 — Identity
- Input:
  - Aggregated signals covering months: domain visit counts (by domain category), saved bookmarks (tag/category), annotated pages (tag), aggregated job-related search queries.
  - Explicit signals (user-provided occupation in settings)
- LLM summarization prompt (template):
  - "You are given sanitized aggregated behavioral features (counts by domain categories, saved items, and repeated search themes across 90 days). Determine stable attributes: occupation, seniority, primary expertise domains, and communication style. Output JSON: {occupation:{title,seniority,confidence}, primary_expertise:[{tag,confidence,evidence_summary}], communication_style:{...}}. No PII. Use confidence 0..1."
- Trigger:
  - Scheduled monthly OR event-based if strong shift detected (e.g., explicit settings change, large increase in job-related visits; delta threshold e.g., new domain with +50% relative activity for 7 days).
- Merge strategy:
  - Weighted merge / conservative overwrite:
    - If new confidence > existing_confidence + 0.15 => overwrite field.
    - If user explicit override exists => do not overwrite.
    - For list fields (expertise): union top-K by confidence; prune lowest confidence to keep size bounded.

L2 — Preferences
- Input:
  - Last 7 days: dwell time vs article length, reading formats engaged, explicit saves/likes, copy actions, explicit settings.
- LLM summarization prompt:
  - "From the following aggregated engagement stats, infer preferred content length, formality, and format preferences. Output JSON with reasons and confidence. Respect explicit overrides."
- Trigger:
  - Weekly scheduled OR immediate when user explicitly sets a preference.
- Merge:
  - Weighted merge favoring recent week; explicit_overrides win. If model_confidence < 0.55, mark preference as tentative and keep previous value.

L3 — Interests (detailed)
- Input:
  - Last 24-48 hours aggregated: top domain categories, clustered search queries (embedding clusters), content interactions (highlights count), bookmarks, time-of-day patterns.
  - Pre-computed embedding clusters (client or server) to group similar signals.
- Pipeline:
  1. Build clusters via cheap algorithm (cosine similarity on query/page embeddings) — small compute.
  2. For each cluster with activity above threshold, call LLM to produce: canonical label, topics list, confidence, intensity, short evidence summary, usage_hints.
- LLM summarization prompt (full example provided below).
- Trigger:
  - Daily scheduled; and on-demand if the user has significant activity that exceeds threshold (e.g., > N domain visits or > M related searches in 12h).
  - Avoid running LLM for users with no activity or whose recent activity delta < threshold.
- Merge strategy:
  - Match new clusters with existing via label or embedding similarity (>0.85):
    - If match: update cluster fields with exponential smoothing:
      new_intensity = alpha * new_intensity + (1-alpha) * old_intensity where alpha = f(recency) (e.g., alpha = 0.6 for same-day).
      new_confidence = max(old_confidence, new_confidence).
      last_activity = max(old,last).
    - If no match and confidence > 0.6: append cluster.
    - Remove clusters with decayed intensity below threshold for > 7 days.

L4 — World Context
- Input:
  - Last 24h: open tabs topics, current session search patterns, task-switching signals (rapid alt-tabs), recent searches, news topics.
- LLM prompt:
  - "Given the recent session signals, produce a compact 'current focus' JSON: active_projects, recent_searches_summary, open_tabs_summary, top news topics. Output short descriptions and relevance score."
- Trigger:
  - Regenerate daily or at session start (assistant invocation). Also regenerate if user opens many tabs on new topic.
- Merge:
  - Overwrite (this is ephemeral). Keep history of last 7 snapshots for temporal smoothing only in memory (not persisted long term).

L5 — Interest Cards
- Purpose: create transient action-oriented suggestions when specific event patterns occur. Cards expire 48h.
- Input:
  - Real-time event patterns (client-side or real-time server detector): search bursts, highlight+followup, bookmark+annotation, multi-clicks to the same topic.
- 3 Concrete trigger patterns (thresholds are tunable; shown here as examples):
  1. Search Burst
     - Pattern: 4+ semantically-similar searches (embedding cosine > 0.85) within a 6-hour window OR 3 searches + 2 clicks to the same topic.
     - Action: create "research" card (title, summary) with recommended actions (save top resources, provide quick summary).
  2. Highlight + Followup
     - Pattern: user highlights text on a page AND within 2 hours performs a follow-up search or opens multiple pages related to that highlighted topic.
     - Action: create "study" card with quick summary, code snippet, or suggested follow-up queries.
  3. Bookmark + Annotate
     - Pattern: user bookmarks a page and attaches a note/annotation or tags it, implying intent to revisit.
     - Action: create "project" card: offer quick actions (add to reading list, set reminder, generate summary).
- Card schema: use the L5 example above.
- Expiry & eviction:
  - Each card has expires_at = created_at + 48 hours (strict).
  - Eviction policy when per-user card count > MAX_CARDS (e.g., 25):
    1. Remove expired cards first.
    2. If still over capacity, evict lowest confidence, then LRU.
  - If a card's topics are absorbed as sustained interest into L3 (confidence > 0.8 and persists > 7 days), optionally convert card to a persistent L3 evidence entry (via scheduled monthly consolidation); do NOT store raw evidence — only summary text.

Merge and update pseudocode (illustrative):
- On L3 update:
  - fetch profile
  - for each new_cluster:
     match = find_existing_cluster_by_embedding_or_label(new_cluster)
     if match:
       match.intensity = alpha * new_cluster.intensity + (1-alpha) * match.intensity
       match.confidence = max(match.confidence, new_cluster.confidence)
       match.last_activity = max(match.last_activity, new_cluster.last_activity)
     else if new_cluster.confidence > 0.6:
       append new_cluster
  - prune clusters with intensity < 0.1 and last_activity older than 7 days

---------------------------------------------------------------------
3) STORAGE AND SERVING ARCHITECTURE
Goals:
- Read P99 latency < 5 ms for profile lookups.
- 10M users, ~2KB per profile → ~20GB primary dataset (plus overhead).
- Writes are async/eventual; reads synchronous.

Recommended design (production-ready choices):
- Primary low-latency store: Redis Enterprise or equivalent in-memory distributed KV with JSON support (RedisJSON). Deploy regional clusters co-located with assistant frontends.
  - Key format: profile:v1:{user_id} => JSON blob with all layers.
  - Use RedisJSON/JSON.GET to fetch selected layer paths (e.g., $.layers.L3_interests.clusters[0:3]) to minimize data transfer.
- Durable persistent store (cold): Azure Cosmos DB / DynamoDB / Bigtable for backup & audit. Writes to durable store are asynchronous and contain only derived profile blobs. This enables rebuilds and debugging while obeying delete semantics.
- Event-processing / work queue: Kafka / Event Hubs for asynchronous update jobs. IMPORTANT: do NOT persist raw behavioral events in this storage. Clients should send only sanitized aggregates to the processing pipeline. Any transient in-memory buffering of raw events must be ephemeral and auto-deleted (policy & enforcement).
- Caching strategy:
  - At the application layer (assistant runtime): small in-process LRU cache (e.g., 10k-100k entries) with TTL = 1–30s for hot users to reduce Redis hops.
  - Primary reads: Redis GET (single hop). Expected Redis GET P99 ~ <1–2 ms in-region; network and app code add ~1–3 ms => target P99 <5 ms achievable with proper co-location.
  - Redis key TTL behavior:
    - L5 cards: set per-card TTL (48h) or store cards with expires_at and rely on Redis expiry.
    - L3/L4 short TTLs on local cache only. Persistent copy in Redis is updated asynchronously.
- Update (write) path (async):
  1. LLM summarizer (worker) produces a layer patch (JSON patch for changed fields) and pushes to update queue.
  2. A writer service consumes queue and applies a merge operation to Redis:
     - Use Redis Lua script to perform atomic read-modify-write/merge logic to avoid race conditions.
     - Writer also pushes profile to durable store (eventually consistent).
  3. On writer success, increment profile.meta.version and set last_updated.
  4. If merge conflicts (concurrent updates), writer either retries or applies deterministic merge (merge priorities per layer).
- Read (sync) path for assistant invocation:
  1. Assistant runtime determines required context subset (L3 top-2 clusters, L2 preferences, L4 world_context) based on query type.
  2. JSON.GET from Redis with path-level fetches (minimize bytes).
  3. Compose prompt snippet and call response LLM (server-side).
  4. If Redis miss (cold), fallback to durable store or default safe profile, mark profile as stale and schedule background reconstruction.
- Scaling estimates:
  - Redis RAM: profiles ~20GB. Allow replication & overhead (indexes): plan ~64GB cluster across nodes for capacity + headroom.
  - With regional clusters and read replicas, Redis GET p99 < 5ms is feasible.

Security & privacy in storage:
- Encrypt at rest & in transit.
- PII redaction applied before write – automatic PII filters (regex + NER classifiers) run in LLM pipeline; if PII detected, redact or ask for user consent.
- Deletion: DELETE API removes Redis key and writes deletion event to durable store and audit log; propagate to backups; ensure backups are purged per retention policy.

APIs (examples)
- GET /profiles/{user_id} — returns profile JSON (user-visible version: only non-sensitive fields).
- DELETE /profiles/{user_id} — deletes profile from Redis and schedules durable store deletion; returns 202 Accepted; propagate purge to replicas/backups within SLA (e.g., 24-72h).
- GET /profiles/{user_id}?layer=L3 — partial fetch (fast).

---------------------------------------------------------------------
4) LLM SUMMARIZATION PIPELINE (detailed)
High-level flow:
1. Client-side (Edge) performs event sanitization & aggregation (preferred): produce aggregated feature payloads (topic counts, top search keywords, highlight ngrams, domain counts, timestamps).
   - This reduces server exposure to raw logs (meets "zero raw behavioral data stored" requirement).
2. Events aggregated into per-user feature records in an ephemeral aggregator (sliding windows).
3. Lightweight clustering/embedding stage (cheap): produce clusters of similar queries/pages.
4. LLM summarization stage: only the sanitized aggregate + cluster summaries are passed to LLM.
5. LLM outputs structured JSON. Post-processors validate, detect PII, and merge per layer rules.
6. Writer service atomically updates Redis (async).

Event batching
- Maintain sliding windows per user:
  - L3: 24 h window, batch once per day OR when activity delta > threshold.
  - L2: weekly aggregator from last 7 days.
  - L1: monthly aggregation of last 90 days.
- To reduce LLM calls at scale:
  - Only run LLM for users who meet "activity threshold" (e.g., >3 domain visits on new topic OR >2 meaningful interactions).
  - Otherwise, use heuristic update: update intensity counters & decay old values without LLM call.
- For L5 (cards): run detector in near real-time (server-side rule engine) using aggregated signals sent by client or a streaming detector.

Summarization model choices (cost v. quality)
- Use a two-tier/three-tier strategy:
  - High-quality model (monthly / heavy): "HQ-LLM" (GPT-4-class / 70B) for L1 and complex merges where correctness is critical.
  - Medium model (daily): "Mid-LLM" (GPT-4o-mini / 13B) for L3/L4 summarization. Lower cost, lower latency.
  - Small model / deterministic rules: for L5 card generation and sanity checks (7B) or deterministic heuristics to reduce cost.
- Recommendation: label-only and short JSON outputs → set temperature=0 and limit tokens. Keep calls deterministic.

Example FULL L3 Prompt (deliverable)
- System instruction:
  "You are a summarization assistant. Input is sanitized aggregated browsing signals (no raw logs, no PII). Produce a JSON object named 'interests' containing up to 6 interest clusters. Each cluster must have: cluster_id, label (<=5 words), topics (list of short tags), confidence (0.0-1.0), intensity (0.0-1.0), last_activity (ISO), decay_half_life_days (int), sample_evidence_summary ( <= 30 words ), usage_hints (1-3 short strings). Output only valid JSON. If uncertain, set confidence <= 0.5. DO NOT include any PII (emails, phone numbers, names)."
- User payload (sanitized example provided inline):
  {
    "time_window":"last_24h",
    "top_domains":[ {"domain":"github.com","visits":10},{"domain":"huggingface.co","visits":6} ],
    "clustered_searches":[ {"cluster_id":"q-1","keywords":["fine-tune llama","LoRA"],"count":4, "top_query":"how to fine-tune llama"} ],
    "highlights":[ {"text_summary":"LoRA reduces fine-tuning params by low-rank adapters", "count":1} ],
    "bookmarks":[ {"tag":"ml_tutorials","count":1} ],
    "session_metrics": { "active_minutes":120, "peak_hour":"10:00-13:00" }
  }
- Assistant instruction:
  "Produce JSON: { 'interests': [ {..clusters..} ] }"

Example expected output (valid JSON only):
{
  "interests":[
    {
      "cluster_id":"c-1029",
      "label":"Transformer Fine-Tuning",
      "topics":["fine-tuning","LoRA","Hugging Face"],
      "confidence":0.95,
      "intensity":0.88,
      "last_activity":"2026-04-18T11:15:00Z",
      "decay_half_life_days":7,
      "sample_evidence_summary":"4 related searches, visit to huggingface.co, highlighted LoRA article",
      "usage_hints":["Show short how-to snippets","Offer repo links and code examples"]
    }
  ]
}

Output parsing & validation
1. Strict JSON schema validation (Ajv / jsonschema):
   - Enforce types, presence of required fields, value ranges.
2. PII detection:
   - Run regex (emails, phones, SSNs) + NER classifier over output strings.
   - If PII found: either (a) mask redacted tokens and lower confidence OR (b) re-run LLM with explicit 'REDUCT PII' instruction.
3. If output is not valid JSON:
   - Re-ask with "Fix only the JSON; output only the JSON" re-prompt up to N retries (N=2).
4. If retries fail:
   - Fallback: keep previous layer data with decayed intensity; log the failure for monitoring.
5. After validated JSON:
   - Normalize labels against canonical taxonomy (fuzzy match using embeddings); map synonyms -> canonical tag.
   - Attach metadata: model_used, model_version, model_confidence, parse_status.
6. Atomic write:
   - Producer writes patch to update queue with desired merge strategy metadata; writer service applies atomic Lua merge against Redis.

Failure handling
- LLM call errors (timeouts, 5xx): exponential backoff & retry up to 2-3 times; if still failing, mark layer update attempt failed and use stale profile; alert ops if error rate high.
- Garbage outputs: detect via schema validator; attempt structured re-prompt; if still invalid, fallback to previous value and mark last_update_failed=True in meta.
- Overuse/cost protections:
  - Circuit breaker: if call-fail rate high or cost budget exceeded, switch to cheaper model or deterministic heuristics until fixed.
- Monitoring & observability:
  - Track per-layer latency, failure rate, token usage, and model drift metrics.

Privacy & PII enforcement
- LLM output must pass automated PII detectors before storage.
- If LLM suggests or infers explicit personal identifiers not in allowed consent (name, email, phone, address), the system strips & marks the inference as invalid.
- Provide user-facing scrubbed profile (for view API) that hides redacted fields and shows reasons.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
5) EVALUATION FRAMEWORK
Goal: measure profile quality, usefulness for personalization, and privacy safety.

Offline evaluation
- Datasets:
  - Use consented ground-truth datasets (surveys + annotated interests) from opt-in users.
  - Synthetic testcases: simulate browser sessions with known ground truth.
- Metrics:
  - For interests (L3): Precision@K, Recall@K, nDCG, cluster labeling accuracy (human-annotated), calibration of confidence (Brier score).
  - For preferences (L2): %match with explicit settings (if user provided), classification accuracy of formality/length.
  - Reconstruction tests: how well derived profile predicts held-out actions (next-day search topic probability): AUC, log-loss.
  - Model robustness: % of outputs with PII (should be 0), rate of JSON parse errors, ratio of failed re-prompts.
- Periodic human evaluation:
  - Sampled human raters judge correctness & usefulness of summaries and evidence summaries.

Online evaluation (production)
- Primary product metrics:
  - Assistant Helpfulness Rate (AHR): % interactions rated helpful (thumbs-up).
  - Task Success Rate: conversion of user intent to completed tasks (e.g., user follows recommended action).
  - Time-to-first-action: median time from suggestion to click/consumption.
  - Engagement: CTR on recommended actions/cards.
- Safety & privacy metrics (guardrails):
  - PII-flag rate: fraction of profile updates flagged by PII-detectors.
  - Delete requests: # profile deletions per 1k users (abnormal spikes need investigation).
  - User opt-outs: % of users opting out of profile personalization.
- System metrics:
  - LLM latency and cost per update; read latency p99 (<5ms).
  - Failure / fallback rates for LLM summarizations.

A/B testing
- Experiment design:
  - Randomize users into: Control (no derived profile personalization), Light (only L3 used for small personalization), Full (all layers & cards enabled).
  - Primary outcome: change in AHR or Task Success Rate over a 2–4 week period.
  - Secondary outcomes: session length, CTR on suggestions, user deletion/opt-out rates, PII flags.
  - Safety monitoring: early stop if negative signals (downgrade in AHR or privacy incidents) exceed threshold.
- Statistical power:
  - Example: baseline helpfulness 60%, detect 2% absolute lift with 80% power → require ~25k users per arm (exact number depends on variance). Run sample-size calculators per business requirement.
- KPI guardrails:
  - Ensure no increased rate of explicit user complaints, no rate of PII exposure, monitor fairness and segmentation (ensuring personalization does not degrade experience for any demographic).

Privacy compliance checks
- Automated PII detection on every LLM output; block/redact any PII unless explicit consent is recorded.
- Logging & auditing:
  - Keep audit logs of profile changes (derived diffs), model versions, and deletion events. Audit logs must not include raw behavioral data.
- Right-to-delete:
  - DELETE /profiles/{user_id} removes derived profile from Redis and schedules deletion from durable stores + backup purge per SLA.
- Data minimization:
  - Keep profile fields small, avoid storing raw text or raw URLs.
- Consent:
  - UI must show what signals are used and allow opt-out. For any PII inference use explicit consent flows before storing.
- Periodic privacy review: run sampling-based human audits to detect unauthorized PII retention.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
6) OPEN QUESTIONS & TRADEOFFS (callouts)
1. LLM cost vs Freshness:
   - Running full LLM summarization for every user daily is expensive (10M * daily calls = untenable). Mitigation: only run LLM when activity crosses thresholds; use cheap embedding clustering + label-only LLM calls; tiered model usage.
   - Tradeoff: lower LLM frequency reduces freshness of interests but saves cost.

2. How much pre-processing on client vs server?
   - Client-side pre-aggregation reduces raw data transmitted to servers (privacy advantage) but increases client complexity and may hurt signal fidelity. Decision: require client-side sanitized aggregates by default; fall back to server-aggregation only with explicit consent.

3. Storing domain vs full URL vs content snippets:
   - Domain-level storage is safer and smaller but less precise. Full URLs or snippets are more informative but increase privacy risk and storage cost. Recommended: store domain+topic tags, not raw page content.

4. PII false positives vs over-redaction:
   - Aggressive PII filters may redact benign text (reducing personalization quality). Need calibrated classifiers and human audits.

5. User control granularity:
   - How much can users edit? Expose safe editing UI (change occupation, remove interest clusters). If user edits, treat as explicit_override and prevent automatic overwrite.

6. Cross-device consistency & cache invalidation:
   - Profiles are per-user and accessed across devices; ensure last-updated & versioning to prevent stale merges. Use optimistic concurrency and atomic merge scripts, but conflicts might still occur for near-simultaneous writes.

7. Legal & compliance:
   - Ensure regional deployments for data residency, and vary retention policies per jurisdiction.

8. Profiling fairness:
   - Need to monitor that inferred interests/preferences do not amplify bias or degrade experience for minorities; implement fairness checks.

---------------------------------------------------------------------
Implementation checklist / Milestones
1. Build sanitized client aggregator library (Edge): local feature extraction, topic tagging, opt-in consent UI.
2. Implement ephemeral aggregator & clustering service (server) that accepts sanitized features.
3. Implement Redis cluster with JSON support and writer service (Lua scripts for atomic merges).
4. Implement LLM pipeline & model routing (HQ vs Mid vs Small models).
5. Implement PII detection + output validator + re-prompt logic.
6. Build card rule engine for L5 triggers + TTL eviction in Redis.
7. Build user-facing APIs to view/export/delete derived profile and UI to edit explicit overrides.
8. Run offline evaluation on opt-in users; tune thresholds; run small-scale A/B tests and ramp.

Appendix: Example merge weight settings (tunable defaults)
- L3 cluster smoothing alpha = 0.6 (recent -> 60%), older -> 40%
- L1 overwrite threshold = new_confidence > old_confidence + 0.15
- L2 tentative cutoff = model_confidence < 0.55 => do not overwrite explicit setting
- L5 card TTL = 48 hours; per-user max cards = 25

---------------------------------------------------------------------
Final note
This design is engineered for low-latency serving, privacy (no raw logs persisted), and cost-aware LLM usage through hybrid pipelines (cheap clustering + targeted LLM labeling). The biggest operational tradeoffs are: (A) LLM cost vs update frequency; (B) client-side aggregation complexity vs server visibility; (C) conservative PII redaction vs personalization fidelity. Each should be iterated on in early pilots with strong privacy audit and human-in-the-loop review before large-scale rollout.
